items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to designating Little Whaley lake, Nuclear lake, Sunset lake, Sylvan lake, Whaley lake and Willow lake as inland waterways for purposes of waterfront revitalization
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4243

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the executive law, in relation to
designating Little Whaley lake, Nuclear lake, Sunset lake, Sylvan
lake, Whaley lake and Willow lake as inland waterways for purposes of
waterfront revitalization

 PURPOSE :

Designates Little Whaley, Nuclear, Sunset, Sylvan, Whaley and Willow
lakes as inland waterways for purposes of waterfront revitalization.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 4 of section 911 of
the executive law, regarding the definition of "inland waterways", by
adding the following lakes: Little Whaley, Nuclear, Sunset (in the
county of Dutchess), Sylvan, Whaley and Willow.

Section two establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The Fishkill Creek watershed is the second largest in Dutchess County.
Situated between the Tenmile River Basin, the only part of New York
that drains into the Housatonic River (which empties into the Long
Island Sound) to the north and east and the Great Swamp Basin, the
headwaters of the New York City's water supply to the south and east,
it is one of the most environmentally sensitive watersheds in New York
State. The creek is also a popular recreational tourism and fishing
destination and is interconnected to the groundwater system throughout
Dutchess County.

Within the watershed, there are also around 1,575 acres of lakes. Its
largest, Whaley Lake, is also the largest in Dutchess County, while
its second largest, Sylvan Lake, is the deepest in the county. Both
are popular recreational fishing and boating locations surrounded by
local development. The Department of Environmental Conservation's
Waterbody Inventory/Priority Waterbodies List, as well as the Natural
Resources Management Plan For The Fishkill Creek Watershed developed
by the Fishkill Creek Watershed Committee, have identified both
significant and minor impacts in the Fishkill Creek basin at these
lakes and others including Little Whaley Lake, Nuclear Lake, Sunset
Lake and Willow Lake.

High chloride concentrations, increased sewage inputs, impacts on
aquatic life from cold water fishery, a lack of adequate stormwater
runoff infrastructure and mesotrophic conditions, which sometimes
approach eutrophic levels due to the over-abundance of nutrients, are
just a few of the issues that plague these lakes, which are critical
to the economic and ecological health and vitality of the
municipalities in which they are located.

By designating these important lakes as inland waterways,
municipalities can align their use with the State's Coastal and Inland
Waterway Policies, and will be able to pursue our shared goals of
improved water quality, preservation of open space and wildlife
habitat, promotion of tourism and economic development opportunities,
as well as combating the aforementioned threats to the Fishkill Creek
watershed.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None of the state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
